approvedEdges.reason: Both records are the 4th-dynasty king Khafre/Chephren: prenomen Cha'ef-rê equals kha.ef ra, and Leprohon's Horus name Weser-ib corroborates the identification.
Both records denote Khafre of Dynasty 4: the shared prenomen Khafra/Cha'ef-rê is corroborated by Record B's Horus name Userib; differing reign dates reflect chronological conventions.
Throne name Men-kaw-rê matches men kau ra, both Dynasty 4; Greek 'Mykerinos' is the standard rendering of Menkaure, corroborated by Horus name Ka-khet.
Both records are 4th-Dynasty Menkaura/Mykerinos with matching throne name Men-kaw-Rê (Men kau Ra); differing reign dates reflect source conventions, not distinct kings.
Prenomen Mer-en-rê/mery-en-Ra and nomen Nemti-em-saf/nemty-em-za.ef both match within Dynasty 6, with Horus Ankhkhau confirming Merenre I.
Both records denote Sixth Dynasty king Nemtiemsaf I: nomen, Merenre prenomen, and Horus name Ankhkhau all match; the minor reign-date difference is convention-relative, not identifying.
Same 6th Dynasty king: identical prenomen Nefer-ka-rê and Pepi II's attested Horus name Netjeri-khau corroborate the match beyond display-name similarity.
Same 6th-dynasty king: nomen Pepi II and prenomen Neferkare agree, and record B's Horus name Netjerikhau is attested for Pepi II; overlapping reign windows reflect only chronological convention.
Shared prenomen Nebhepetre, matching nomen Mentuhotep, and Horus name Netjeri-Hedjet all corroborate one king; Leprohon's '(b)' marks an attestation variant of Mentuhotep II.
Same Dynasty 11 king: matching prenomen Nebhepetre and Horus name Sema-tawy, with agreeing nomen Mentuhotep, corroborate identity beyond display-name similarity.
Both records share 11th-dynasty prenomen Nebhepetre and nomen Mentuhotep II, with Record B's Horus names matching his titulary; differing reign dates merely reflect chronological conventions.
Shared prenomen Sankhkare plus unique Horus name Sankhtawyef and 11th-dynasty Mentuhotep nomen confirm both records denote Mentuhotep III.

Both records share the unique 11th-dynasty prenomen Sankhkare/Se'anch-ka-rê for Mentuhotep III, corroborated by dynasty and nomen; differing reign dates reflect chronological conventions, not distinct kings.
Both records share the distinctive 11th Dynasty prenomen Nebtawyre and Horus name Nebtawy for Mentuhotep IV; the ~36-year date gap reflects differing chronological conventions, not distinct kings.
Both records agree on 12th Dynasty king Amenemhat I with prenomen Sehetep-ib-Rê, corroborated by Horus name Sehetep-ib-tawy in record B.
Same Dynasty 12 king: both give prenomen Sehetep-ib-Ra and nomen Amenemhat I, with Leprohon adding Horus name Wehem-mesut, matching Amenemhat I's attested titulary.

Both records are 12th-Dynasty Amenemhat I: matching prenomen Sehetepibre and nomen Amenemhat, with Horus name Sehetepib-tawy corroborating; differing reign dates reflect chronological conventions, not distinct kings.
Same Dynasty 12 king: matching prenomen Kheperkare plus Horus name Ankhmesut corroborates Senwosret I / Sesostris I despite name-form variation.
